A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 34-page versions of Gaze-VLM, including Appendix A. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish that the same research content is available throughout.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations on Ego4D and EGTEA+ Gaze, a 200-example human hallucination evaluation, and appendix ablations and STA benchmark results.

after.justification: v2 retains the original model evaluations, human-evaluation outcomes and appendix experiments, including the numerical STA results in Table 21.

M1.justification: The gaze aggregation, occlusion filtering, attention regularization, training objective and RGB-only inference procedures in Section 3 and Appendices A.3-A.4 are identical.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same Ego4D and EGTEA+ Gaze coverage, including fine-grained prediction, activity understanding, static-image understanding, coarse narration prediction and the predicted-gaze STA experiment.

E2.justification: The five architecture-based comparisons in Table 1, pretrained InternVL and OpenFlamingo comparators in Table 8, and appendix control variants are unchanged.

E3.justification: Sampling, observation and anticipation horizons, evaluation metrics, training settings and human-evaluation procedures remain identical. The punctuation added in A.5.2 does not revise the evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same regularization, temporal-window, gaze-representation, occlusion and attention-component ablations, alongside unchanged generalization, hallucination, alignment and failure-case analyses.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged. Both report the same point estimates without supplying repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or formal significance tests; the checklist's significance statement is also identical.

E6.justification: All numerical and qualitative results are unchanged. Table 1 retains OpenFlamingo future-prediction scores of 0.6525 for the base model and 0.7505 with gaze regularization; Table 21 retains STA noun mAP values of 22.13 and 25.01.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and formulations in Equations (1)-(11) are identical. Neither version contains formal theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about training-only gaze supervision, modularity, improved egocentric understanding and prediction, and reduced hallucinations.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and qualifications are identical, including Appendix A.6's limitations concerning temporal downsampling, motion blur and gaze calibration.

D1.justification: Annotation prompts, occlusion thresholds, hardware, training hyperparameters, runtime details and code/data access statements are unchanged. The appendix punctuation edits disclose no new technical information.

R1.justification: Section 2, Appendix A.1 and the references retain the same cited works and research positioning. The updated conference notice changes publication information rather than the relationship to prior research.

P1.justification: v2 replaces 'Preprint. Under review.' with the NeurIPS 2025 conference notice, updates the arXiv version/date stamp, and adds sentence-ending periods in A.3, A.5.1 and A.5.2. The remaining wording and document structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1-10, Tables 1-21 and both algorithms retain their displays, captions, formatting and placement. Page layout is unchanged; the first-page notice and stamp edits only replace text.

improvement.justification: The publication-information updates and three added periods provide negligible editorial polish. Scientific content, supporting evidence, reproducibility information and substantive presentation remain identical, establishing no meaningful net difference in overall quality.
